page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the AMD EPYC-powered N2D family. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio, which is tailored for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and compression tasks fall within the average range. Specifically, the instance achieves a stress-ng multi-core score of 21,558.27 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,379.0. Memory read-only bandwidth reaches 1,018.3 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 75.4 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks, while write bandwidth is measured at 40.36 GB/sec.

For specialized workloads, the instance delivers average performance across database operations, web serving, and lightweight machine learning tasks. Redis SET operations reach 16.05 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 15.62 GB/sec. Large language model inference using a small 135M model yields 904.0 tokens per second for prompt processing and 242.73 tokens per second for text generation. The hardware supports AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets, enhancing cryptographic and integer calculation efficiency.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highcpu-16 offers a resource-dense configuration for CPU-bound tasks, minimizing memory overhead costs. The primary tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and the lack of local storage, which requires external block storage attachment. It is highly suitable for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, batch processing, and lightweight cryptographic operations.
